canonical.title: Proxmox as the isolation boundary for Claude Code: KVM VM, not LXC

parent.title: Running Claude Code safely on a Linux workstation, and where Proxmox actually helps

siblings.title: Threat model and blast radius: what actually goes wrong running an agentic coding CLI on your workstation
siblings.summary: The realized 2026 losses come from the agent's own destructive git commands and from supply-chain malware that weaponizes an installed agent CLI — not from the exotic prompt-injection scenarios; containment must stop out-of-workspace writes, egress, and credential reads, in that order.

siblings.title: Claude Code's native guardrails in 2026: what the permission model holds, and where it stops
siblings.summary: Claude Code's permission rules are an in-process policy layer, not a security boundary; only the bubblewrap-backed Bash sandbox has OS teeth, and it covers Bash alone — here is the exact syntax, the documented holes, the CVEs, and the two controls that hold in every mode.

siblings.title: Linux-native sandboxing for Claude Code on the workstation itself
siblings.summary: Turn on Claude Code's built-in bubblewrap sandbox, then wrap the whole process in a 30-line bwrap script; systemd-run --user, firejail and Flatpak are the wrong tools for this job, and Landlock is the primitive to bet on but not to hand-roll.

siblings.title: Containers as the containment layer for `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`
siblings.summary: Rootless Podman plus a proxy-only internal network beats Anthropic's reference devcontainer; the reference firewall leaks DNS and hands the agent NET_ADMIN.

siblings.title: Credential isolation for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: An agent that can read $HOME holds your whole identity, and on Linux the keyring does not help — so give the agent its own short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials instead.

siblings.title: Audit trail and recovery drills for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: Git commits are your real undo and a PostToolUse hook is your real audit log — Claude Code's own transcripts and /rewind are convenience layers that expire, miss bash, and are writable by the agent.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Wiki — Linux Container
sources.claim: Containers share the host kernel; full VMs provide better isolation. Unprivileged containers map container root to an unprivileged host UID. FUSE inside containers is strongly discouraged.

sources.title: LXC — Security
sources.claim: LXC upstream's position: privileged containers aren't and cannot be root-safe; unprivileged containers are safe by design.

sources.title: Claude Code Docs — Sandbox environments
sources.claim: Anthropic recommends a dedicated VM for untrusted repositories: own kernel, kernel-level separation.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Docs — Firewall
sources.claim: The Proxmox firewall is a host-side iptables service per node with cluster/host/guest levels; must be enabled at datacenter level and per network device.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Docs — Storage
sources.claim: ZFS and LVM-thin snapshot natively at block level; internal qcow2 snapshots block a running VM and can take minutes to hours.

sources.title: Proxmox Forum — Docker in unprivileged LXC or dedicated VM
sources.claim: Docker inside LXC is unsupported and may break; use QEMU/KVM VMs for Docker for best isolation.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Docs — Proxmox Container Toolkit
sources.claim: Nesting containers inside a QEMU VM is recommended for maximum isolation; never bind mount system directories into a container.

sources.title: Docker on Proxmox LXC: what actually works and why unprivileged doesn't
sources.claim: Docker does not work in unprivileged LXC on current Proxmox kernels; the privileged workaround is a performance choice, not a security choice. VM overhead ~200 MB plus a boot delay.

sources.title: Proxmox Forum — Root Docker in unprivileged LXC, safe or not?
sources.claim: Proxmox staff: it can still be possible to break out of the LXC when nesting is enabled.

sources.title: Hacker News — How are you sandboxing your coding agents?
sources.claim: Practitioner approaches range from fully airgapped separate systems to dockerized git worktrees, with widespread dissatisfaction about friction.

sources.title: Hacker News — 2026 agent sandboxing survey thread
sources.claim: The field splits mainly between containers and minimal isolation, with a minority on KVM/QEMU VMs plus SSH and dedicated unprivileged accounts.

sources.title: Northflank — How to sandbox AI agents
sources.claim: Standard containers are insufficient for untrusted code; Firecracker microVMs boot in ~125 ms with under 5 MiB overhead per VM.

sources.title: Quantifying Frontier LLM Capabilities for Container Sandbox Escape (arXiv)
sources.claim: Academic work measures frontier-model capability at identifying and exploiting container misconfigurations to escape sandboxes.

sources.title: Microsoft Security — Postinstall payload inside the Mastra npm supply-chain compromise
sources.claim: 140+ packages poisoned with a dayjs typosquat whose postinstall hook ran an obfuscated dropper that disabled TLS verification and harvested developer credentials and tokens.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Wiki — System Requirements
sources.claim: Minimum 1 GB RAM; recommended 2 GB for the OS and PVE services plus designated guest memory; ~1 GB per TB of used storage for ZFS.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Wiki — ZFS on Linux
sources.claim: PVE 8.1+ defaults ARC to 10% of host memory clamped to 16 GiB; sizing rule is 2 GiB base plus 1 GiB per TiB of pool; older installs may be uncapped.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Docs — Qemu/KVM Virtual Machines
sources.claim: Min memory equal to max allocates directly instead of ballooning; ballooning under pressure can trigger guest swap or the OOM killer; VirtIO SCSI single with IO thread is current best practice; discard shrinks thin images.

sources.title: VS Code Docs — Remote Development FAQ
sources.claim: VS Code Server runs as the user you signed in with; workspace extensions get full access to the source code, remote filesystem and remote APIs. Needs kernel >= 4.18, glibc >= 2.28.

sources.title: VS Code Docs — Developing with Remote Tunnels
sources.claim: code tunnel makes outbound connections to a Microsoft service hosted in Azure and requires the same GitHub or Microsoft account on both ends.

sources.title: JetBrains — Remote development prerequisites
sources.claim: For larger projects add CPUs and RAM, enable swap, and use local SSD storage; single-board computers and shared hosting are unsupported.

sources.title: Mosh (mobile shell)
sources.claim: Survives roaming and laptop sleep, provides local echo, runs over UDP 60000-61000, and authenticates by logging in over SSH first.

sources.title: rogs.me — Claude Code from the beach: mosh, tmux and ntfy
sources.claim: A February 2026 practitioner setup: mosh for connection resilience, tmux for session persistence with auto-attach on login, Claude Code hooks pushing ntfy notifications.

sources.title: Claude Code Docs — Headless mode
sources.claim: claude -p runs the agent loop non-interactively; --output-format json returns result, session_id and total_cost_usd; --bare skips auto-discovery for reproducible runs.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Docs — qm(1)
sources.claim: qm snapshot takes an optional --vmstate for RAM; qm rollback does not start the VM unless --start is passed; qm guest exec runs commands via the guest agent.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Docs — pct(1)
sources.claim: Containers use the same snapshot verbs as VMs (pct snapshot / rollback --start / listsnapshot / delsnapshot); pct exec and pct enter run commands from the host.

sources.title: Proxmox Forum — virtiofs shared host folder for guest VMs
sources.claim: virtiofs exposes host filesystem permissions directly, blocks live migration, and community testing finds it significantly slower than NFS.

sources.title: NAS performance: SSHFS vs NFS vs SMB
sources.claim: NFS dominates small random 4K operations and is fastest in plaintext; SSHFS is the fastest encrypted option.

sources.title: Proxmox Forum — Snapshot VM question: RAM / no RAM
sources.claim: Snapshots without RAM roll back as if the guest suffered a power outage; snapshots with RAM write a vmstate volume the size of guest memory (~21 GB observed).

sources.title: Proxmox VE Wiki — QEMU guest agent
sources.claim: Enabled with qm set VMID --agent 1; calls guest-fsfreeze-freeze and guest-fsfreeze-thaw around backups and snapshots to improve consistency.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Wiki — Network Configuration
sources.claim: A Linux bridge is a virtual switch; bridge-vlan-aware yes makes per-guest VLAN tags work transparently; bridge-ports none creates an isolated guest network.

sources.title: Proxmox VE Wiki — Software-Defined Network
sources.claim: An SDN Simple zone creates an isolated VNet bridge not linked to a physical interface, with traffic local to each node.

sources.title: Proxmox Forum — Isolated private networks with SDN
sources.claim: SDN Simple zones do not isolate guests by default because they lack a dedicated VRF; real isolation requires layered Proxmox firewall rules.

sources.title: CyLab — Building isolated network topologies in Proxmox
sources.claim: Recipe using SDN VNets plus an OPNsense router VM: a NIC per VNet, static gateway IPs, DHCP/DNS, interface-based firewall rules.

sources.title: Teleport — What is SSH X11 forwarding?
sources.claim: Trusted X11 forwarding lets a malicious remote capture keystrokes, manipulate other windows, read and write the clipboard, and screenshot the display.

sources.title: Clockwork — SSH agent hijacking
sources.claim: Anyone with root on a remote host can use a forwarded agent socket to authenticate as you elsewhere without touching your private key files.

sources.title: GitHub Docs — Managing deploy keys
sources.claim: A deploy key grants access to a single repository, read-only by default, private half staying on the server; no passphrase and no expiry.

sources.title: VirtualizationHowto — Proxmox cloud-init made easy
sources.claim: Concrete qm command sequence for building a cloud-init template and cloning it to a working VM.

sources.title: Proxmox — Virtual Environment 9.2 press release
sources.claim: PVE 9.2 released 21 May 2026 on Debian 13.5 with kernel 7.0, QEMU 11.0, LXC 7.0 and ZFS 2.4.

sources.title: Claude Code Docs — Sandboxing
sources.claim: Sandboxing is not a complete isolation boundary; broad domain allowlists enable exfiltration because the proxy does not inspect TLS; docker.sock grants host access; --dangerously-skip-permissions is blocked as root.

sources.title: im404 — Isolated development environments with Proxmox LXC
sources.claim: Per-language Proxmox LXC dev environments over VS Code Remote-SSH; the benefit is dependency isolation rather than security.

sources.title: Proxmox Forum — VM or LXC?
sources.claim: LXC framed as a semi-isolated environment that can leak or interfere with the host under extreme conditions.

sources.title: swatinem.de — Optimizing tsc
sources.claim: tsc heap usage scales with type surface: 61 MB on an empty project versus 465 MB with aws-sdk types in scope; large projects run close to the Node memory limit.
